answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring a stake that is burned on proven misbehavior, like a marble held in escrow: each identity must lock value before it can transact, so creating a thousand fake agents costs a thousand stakes. The ledger keeps a small ember of reputation history per identity, and new identities start in a slow oasis of limited trust, earning full access only after sustained honest work. A bot farm pays real capital for every copy, while honest agents pay once.
